body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Yuktiṣaṣṭikākārikā</s> (Sixty Verses on Reasoning). Homage to the youthful <s>Mañjuśrī</s>.

children.translated_text: Homage to that chief of sages who taught dependent [arising] (<s>pratītyopāda</s>),
by whom, through this method, both arising and destruction are negated.
Those whose understanding transcends existence and non-existence, unsupported [by either] —
by them, the deep, supportless meaning of conditions is perceived. (verse 1)
Non-existence, the source of all faults, has been refuted;

children.text: nirvartyate yathā yuktayā bhāvo 'pi śrvavaṇaṃ kuru || Yukti_2
children.translated_text: how existence too is refuted through reasoning — listen. (verse 2)
If existence were real, as imagined by the childish,

children.text: vimokṣastadabhāvena ko necchet kim na kārnāt || Yukti_3
children.translated_text: liberation through its absence — who would not want it, and for what reason [would they not]? (verse 3)

children.text: vimokṣo nāsti bhāvena bhāvo nāsti hyabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Liberation does not [come] through [real] existence; existence does not [arise] from non-existence;
through the full understanding (<s>parijñāna</s>) of both existence and non-existence, the great one (<s>mahātmā</s>) is liberated. (verse 4)

children.text: nirvāṇam caiva lokaṃ ca manyante tattvadarśinaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and the world — seers of reality (<s>tattvadarśin</s>) regard [neither];

children.text: naiva lokaṃ na nirvānaṃ manyante tattvadarśinaḥ || Yukti_5
children.translated_text: neither the world nor <s>nirvāṇa</s> — seers of reality regard [neither]. (verse 5)

children.text: nirvānaṃ ca bhavaścaiva dvayameva na vidyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and existence — this duality does not exist at all;
the full understanding of existence itself is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. (verse 6)
Just as cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is imagined for an entity that has the capacity for arising,
so the wise regard this cessation as produced by illusion (<s>māyā</s>). (verse 7)

children.text: samskṛto na parijñāto nirodho vibhave sati |
children.translated_text: The conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), not fully understood, [has its] cessation when capacity exists;

children.text: pratyakṣam bhūyate kasmin vibhavo jñāyate katham || Yukti_8
children.translated_text: in what is it made manifest? How is its capacity known? (verse 8)
If through the cessation of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) there would be no exhaustion of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>),

children.text: yadā cāyaṃ niruddhaḥ syāttadā mokṣo bhavisyati || Yukti_9
children.translated_text: then when these [aggregates] have ceased, at that time liberation will [supposedly] come about. (verse 9)
For one who sees with right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) what has arisen from the condition of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>),
neither arising nor cessation is found to be justified. (verse 10)

children.text: evam paśyati dharmaḥ yo nirvānam vā katam tathā |
children.translated_text: One who thus sees <s>dharma</s>, or <s>nirvāṇa</s> likewise —

children.text: dharmajñānam paraṃ yatra bhedastu tatra vidyate || Yukti_11
children.translated_text: where there is supreme <s>dharma</s>-knowledge, there differentiation still exists. (verse 11)
One who imagines the birth of an extremely subtle entity
does not see the meaning that arises from conditions — he is undiscerning. (verse 12)
If <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) whose defilements (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) are exhausted are prevented from <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: kutaḥ sampannabuddhaiśca tasyārambho na bhāṣitaḥ || Yukti_13
children.translated_text: why was its beginning not declared by those of accomplished wisdom (<s>sammannabuddha</s>)? (verse 13)
If there were a beginning, there would be the grasping of a one-sided view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>);

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādastasya purvaṃ paraṃ vā kim || Yukti_14
children.translated_text: for <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising) — what is prior or subsequent to it? (verse 14)
How is what has arisen first prevented afterwards?
Liberation, devoid of beginning and end, is renowned as illusion-like (<s>māyopama</s>). (verse 15)

children.text: bhavatīdam yadā māyā namkṣyatīti tadaiva hi |
children.translated_text: When this comes into being, it is [already] illusion; when it perishes, it is illusion indeed;
overcome by the illusion of ignorance, deluded by the illusion of ignorance. (verse 16)

children.text: yathā marīcikā māyā bhavam buddhayā hi paśyati |
children.translated_text: One who sees existence with wisdom as a mirage (<s>marīcikā</s>), as illusion (<s>māyā</s>),

children.text: purvāntam vāparāntam vā na dṛṣṭayā parikliśyate || Yukti_17
children.translated_text: is not afflicted by views of a prior or subsequent end. (verse 17)
Those who think the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) involves imagined destruction and arising

children.text: pratītyotpādacakreṇa vijānanti na te jagat || Yukti_18
children.translated_text: do not understand the world through the wheel of dependent arising (<s>pratītyotpādacakra</s>). (verse 18)
What has arisen depending on that has not arisen by itself;

children.text: svayam yadā yadutpannamutpannam nāma tat katham || Yukti_19
children.translated_text: when something has arisen by itself, how can that be called 'arisen'? (verse 19)
Pacified through the destruction of causes alone, it is understood as 'perished';

children.text: svabhāvena hi yatkṣīṇam tat kṣīṇamucyate katham || Yukti_20
children.translated_text: how can what has perished by its own nature be called 'perished'? (verse 20)

children.text: na kaścidanutpannam nirodho 'pi na vai tathā |
children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever is unarisen; cessation too is not [of the unarisen];
the intended meaning regarding the function of arising and destruction has been demonstrated. (verse 21)
From the knowledge of arising [comes the understanding of] destruction; from the knowledge of destruction, impermanence;
from the understanding of impermanence, the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) is indeed awakened. (verse 22)
One who fully understands <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising) as devoid of arising and destruction —
by that very [understanding] the ocean of existence (<s>bhavābdhi</s>) is crossed. (verse 23)
Ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), their self-natures inverted by [concepts of] existent and non-existent,
beings caught in the lineage of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>), deceived by thoughts of self (<s>ātmacitta</s>). (verse 24)
By the wise, entities are contemplated as empty (<s>śūnya</s>), impermanent, without self (<s>anātmaka</s>);
and the accumulation of perishable <s>dharmas</s> is seen as isolated (<s>vivikta</s>). (verse 25)
Due to rootlessness, there is no stability; unsupported (<s>nirālamba</s>), without basis (<s>nirāśraya</s>);
arisen from the cause of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); devoid of beginning, middle, and end. (verse 26)
like a city of delusion (<s>mohapurī</s>) — one who sees the world as illusion-like (<s>māyāvat</s>). (verse 27)
Here even the world from <s>Brahmā</s> onward appears as if real;

children.text: satyanmṛṣetyuktamāryena tatra kā śiṣyate parā || Yukti_28
children.translated_text: 'The real is false' — said the Noble One (<s>Ārya</s>); what other [reality] then remains? (verse 28)
This world, blinded by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), is swept away by the current of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>);
for one who is wise and free from craving, how can there be a view comparable to [that of] merit? || 29 ||
First, having seen this reality, it is declared 'everything exists';
one who knows, though not attached to objects, is later surely discriminated [from the ignorant]. || 30 ||
Those who do not know the discriminated meaning, [but merely] proceed based on hearing alone —
for them, merit is unbroken; other people are destroyed. || 31 ||
Actions endowed with results have been taught; this world [arises] rightly;
but the thorough knowledge of its own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) has been taught as unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>). || 32 ||
'I' and 'mine' are spoken by people according to the force of necessity;
likewise, the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) are taught according to the force of necessity. || 33 ||
The great elements and the like are declared [to exist] in consciousness; likewise the accumulation [of aggregates];

children.text: tajjñānena viyukttena mṛṣaiva na vikalpitam || Yukti_34
children.translated_text: disconnected from the knowledge of that, they are merely falsely — not [truly] — conceptualized. || 34 ||
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> alone is the one truth that the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) declare;

children.text: nāva śiṣṭam tadā satyamevam vijñena kalpitam || Yukti_35
children.translated_text: what remains then is not truth — thus it is conceived by the wise. || 35 ||
As long as there is distraction of the mind, so long is it the domain of <s>Māra</s>;

children.text: evambhūto bhavedyatra nā doṣo jāyate kathaṃ || Yukti_36
children.translated_text: for one who has become thus [free from distraction], in what manner would a fault arise? || 36 ||
Since the world is proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s> to have ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) as its condition,
therefore this world is conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) — how is this not reasonable? || 37 ||
Just as when ignorance is ceased, cessation arises,

children.text: ajñānato hi samkalpa iti kim na vidhīyate || Yukti_38
children.translated_text: [so] from ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) comes conceptual construction (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) — why is this not established? || 38 ||

children.text: hetutaḥ sambhavo yasya sthiti rna pratyayairvinā |
children.translated_text: That whose origination is from causes, whose continued existence is not without conditions,
whose cessation is from the absence of conditions — how is that understood as 'existent'? || 39 ||
If the proponents of [real] existence (<s>bhāvavādins</s>) rely on a supreme entity for [its] continued existence,

children.text: tadaiva hi sthitā mārge na kaściditasmayastataḥ || Yukti_40
children.translated_text: then indeed they stand on the [right] path; therefore no one should be astonished at that. || 40 ||
All who are established on the path of the <s>Buddha</s> are proponents of impermanence (<s>anitya</s>);

children.text: kena vādena gṛhyante bhāvāḥ santi parā iti || Yukti_41
children.translated_text: by what argument are entities grasped as 'they exist as supreme'? || 41 ||
Where the examination 'it is this or that' is not found,

children.text: idam satyamado veti paṇḍitaiḥ kathamucyatai || Yukti_42
children.translated_text: 'this is true, that is not' — how can the wise say [such a thing]? || 42 ||
And without grasping, the world — or the self — desires by those [wise ones];
the arising of [notions of] permanent, impermanent, and the like is abandoned through [abandoning] false views. || 43 ||
For those by whom entities are grasped as realities, their [so-called] truths are established;

children.text: tatra liṅgādayo doṣāḥ prajāyante na vā kathaṃ || Yukti_44
children.translated_text: how do faults such as [false] marks and the like arise therein — or not? || 44 ||

children.text: yān hi dharmānupādāya dṛṣṭaścandro jale yathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> by which [things are] grasped are like the moon [seen reflected] in water;

children.text: tatra satyam mṛṣā naiva kāmaṃ dṛṣṭyā na hāritaḥ || Yukti_45
children.translated_text: therein there is neither truth nor falsity — indeed, one is not carried away by [such a] view. || 45 ||
Fierce clinging to corrupt views arising from passion (<s>rāga</s>) and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>),
and disputes arising from them — [these occur] when there is acceptance of [real] existence (<s>bhāva</s>). || 46 ||

children.text: sa hetuḥ sarvadṛṣṭīnām kleśotpatti rna tam vinā |
children.translated_text: That [acceptance of real existence] is the cause of all views; without it, <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) do not arise;
therefore, when that is thoroughly known, views and afflictions are exhausted. || 47 ||
And by what is [that] thoroughly known? — Through seeing dependent origination (<s>pratītyotpāda</s>);
the best among knowers of reality stated: what is dependently arisen is unborn. || 48 ||
One who, having overcome false knowledge, clings to [what is] untrue as if true —
[for such a one], the grasping of speculation and the like, [leading] in sequence to attachment and action, is recognized. || 49 ||

children.text: mahātmanām na pakṣo vā vitarko vā na vidyate |
children.translated_text: The great souls have neither a thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) nor speculation;

children.text: yeṣām na vidyate pakṣeḥ parapakṣaḥ kutasteṣām || Yukti_50
children.translated_text: for those who have no thesis, how could there be an opposing thesis? || 50 ||
One who has taken refuge in that very [entity] is bitten by the venomous snakes of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: calaṃ vāniṣṭhitam cittaṃ na tiṣṭhatyanāśritam || Yukti_51
children.translated_text: the restless, unsteadfast mind does not remain without a support. || 51 ||

children.text: sāśraya cittavāna sattveḥ kleśodbhūto viṣo mahān |
children.translated_text: For a being with a mind that has a support, the great poison born of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) [is active];

children.text: sadā pṛthagajano hīnaḥ kleśasarpena gṛhītaḥ || Yukti_52
children.translated_text: always the ordinary, ignorant, inferior person is seized by the serpent of afflictions. || 52 ||

children.text: prativimbe yathā rāgo loke ca mohavandhanāt |
children.translated_text: Just as there is passion toward a reflection, in the world, due to the bond of delusion,

children.text: viṣayapinjaro sakto bālo hi satyasamjñayā || Yukti_53
children.translated_text: the fool, confined in the cage of sense-objects, clings with the notion of truth. || 53 ||
One sees objects, so to speak, with the eyes, through the knowledge of the image;
unattached to the mud of <s>karma</s> (action) — such is the nature of the great soul. || 54 ||
Ordinary people, attached to form, are deluded; the middling ones are free from attachment;

children.text: rūpasvabhāvavijño yo vimukto buddhimān paraḥ || Yukti_55
children.translated_text: one who knows the own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of form is liberated, wise, supreme. || 55 ||
Having opened [oneself] from the thought of pleasure, free from the dispassionate and [those not] free from passion,
seeing [the world] like a magical person — such a one will be turned back [from <s>saṃsāra</s>]. || 56 ||
One who is burned by false knowledge and becomes a partaker of the faults of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) —
through conceptualizing existence and non-existence, true knowledge of objects does not arise. || 57 ||
Those who are without support, free from passion, are indeed devoid of attachment;

children.text: arāge rāgavardhāste na sāśrayā mahātmanaḥ || Yukti_58
children.translated_text: Those who are free from attachment — attachment does not increase in them; the great souls have no such attachment.
Those whose minds are secluded — their mind is restless and fickle,
yet even when bitten by the serpent of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), they are sharp and unwearied, [crossing] the ocean of <s>bhava</s> (existence).

children.text: śāstreṇānena janānām punyam jñānam ca sancitam |
children.translated_text: By this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), the merit and knowledge of people are accumulated;
may they, through the arising of meritorious knowledge and action, attain the supreme state.

body.translated_text: Like the pith of a plantain (<s>kadalī</s>), like a city of <s>gandharvas</s>,
Thus the <s>Yuktiṣaṣṭikākārikā</s> (Sixty Verses on Reasoning) is complete.
From the mouth of the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, [this] excellent <s>śāstra</s> (treatise)

children.translated_text: was heard from the Indian <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Muditaśrī</s>
and by the Tibetan resident named <s>Sūryakīrti</s> from the border region,
a Tibetan <s>paṇḍita</s>, it was written in the Tibetan language.
